title: Design a Real-Time Chat System (Slack / WhatsApp)
summary: Design a massively distributed real-time messaging architecture supporting 1-on-1 private messaging, large group channels, presence tracking, and offline push sync.
description: Design a real-time messaging platform supporting 50 million daily active users exchanging hundreds of millions of messages daily. The system must maintain millions of concurrent persistent WebSocket connections, guarantee sub-100ms end-to-end delivery latency, provide strict message ordering within conversations, manage online/offline presence tracking, support rich media attachments, and reliably fall back to mobile push notifications for offline users.
functional_requirements: 1-on-1 Direct Messaging: Private, low-latency messaging between two users with delivery receipts (sent, delivered, read).
Group Chat Channels: Support public and private group channels accommodating up to 10,000 active participants.
Real-Time Presence Tracking: Display online, away, and offline status with low-overhead periodic heartbeats.
Cross-Device Synchronization: Seamless multi-device synchronization keeping unread counts and message history aligned across desktop, web, and mobile.
Media File Sharing: Support image, audio, and document uploads via secure pre-signed URLs and distributed CDN distribution.
Offline Handoff: Deliver notifications via APNs and FCM when recipients are disconnected, backfilling history upon reconnection.
non_functional_requirements: Ultra-low Delivery Latency: P99 end-to-end message transit latency strictly under 100ms for connected clients.
Zero Message Loss & Durability: Messages acknowledged by the server must be durably persisted across multiple availability zones.
Strict Message Ordering: Guarantee casual and chronological sequence ordering within every channel or direct conversation.
High Concurrency: Maintain 10,000,000 simultaneous open WebSocket / TCP socket connections.
High Availability: 99.99% service availability with automatic failover during gateway instance crashes.
key_challenges: Stateful WebSocket connection management: Distributing millions of persistent TCP connections across gateway instances and maintaining a dynamic user-to-server routing table in Redis.
Group fan-out explosion: Mitigating write amplification in large channels by switching from fan-out-on-write to fan-out-on-read with channel sequence cursors.
Distributed message ordering: Generating collision-free 64-bit sequence numbers (Twitter Snowflake) that preserve monotonic time order per conversation without distributed locks.
Presence thundering herd: Handling 10 million heartbeats every 30 seconds without overwhelming Redis or creating broadcast storms on channel presence updates.
Reconnection bursts & offline catch-up: Efficiently fetching unread messages using pagination tokens (`since_message_id`) without causing database connection starvation.

reference_solution.architecture_pattern: Stateful edge connection gateways connected via distributed message fabric to horizontally partitioned NoSQL persistence and ephemeral presence clusters
core_components: Layer 4 TCP Load Balancer routing client traffic across horizontally auto-scaled WebSocket Gateway nodes
WebSocket Gateway Fleet terminating TLS and maintaining bidirectional connections with active clients
Session Registry (Redis Cluster) mapping user_id and device_id to current gateway pod IP addresses
Message Distribution Fabric (Apache Kafka / NATS) routing chat events to target gateway servers and persistence queues
Chat Message Store (Apache Cassandra / ScyllaDB) using partition key `channel_id` and clustering key `message_id DESC` for rapid range retrieval
Presence Service leveraging Redis Sorted Sets and TTL keys with 30-second heartbeat windows
Push Notification Gateway queuing APNs/FCM delivery jobs for offline recipients
Object Storage (Amazon S3 / Google Cloud Storage) behind CloudFront CDN for media attachments
reference_solution.fan_out_model: Hybrid fan-out: Direct messages and small groups (<100 members) push events directly to recipient sockets; large channels broadcast message notifications to connected channel subscribers via Kafka topics, with clients maintaining read offset cursors.
